items.label: f02-materialized-progress-drift
items.front: Trade-off of storing progressPercent instead of computing it on read?
items.back: Reads and sorting are fast (a plain integer column), but every write path that changes tasks must recalculate it, ideally in the same transaction; any path that skips or fails the hook leaves the column stale.

items.label: f01-idor-get-case
items.front: GET /cases/:id has only authMiddleware and fetches the case by raw id. Risk and fix?
items.back: IDOR: any authenticated user can read any department's case by changing the id. Fix: scope the query with the departmentId resolved from the verified session (or require VIEW_ALL_CASES), and add a cross-department security test.

items.label: f04-no-external-calls-in-tx
items.front: Rule for side effects such as emails around a database transaction?
items.back: Keep them out of the transaction: commit first, then enqueue. External latency inside a transaction holds connections and locks, and a side effect cannot be rolled back with the data.

items.label: f03-volatile-job-fallback
items.front: When Redis is offline, notifications fall back to setTimeout in the Node process. Risk and fix?
items.back: Pending jobs die with the process (crash, OOM, autoscale restart): no durability, no retry. In production, refuse to boot without the queue, or sweep PENDING email rows on startup.

Not at all: logout deletes the token server-side, so the next call fails signature verification
Until the user's next login, which rotates JWT_ACCESS_SECRET
For 7 days, because access tokens are issued with the same lifetime as the refresh token

choices: Until the access token expires (15 minutes by default): there is no revocation list
Not at all: logout deletes the token server-side, so the next call fails signature verification
Until the user's next login, which rotates JWT_ACCESS_SECRET
For 7 days, because access tokens are issued with the same lifetime as the refresh token

items.explanation: verifyAccessToken is jwt.verify with the access secret; with no blacklist, a cryptographically valid token works until JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRES_IN (default '15m') elapses.

items.prompt: A case has 6 tasks: 2 COMPLETED, 1 SKIPPED, 2 TODO and 1 PENDING_APPROVAL. What progressPercent does recalculateOnboardingProgress store?
items.explanation: COMPLETED and SKIPPED both count as done: 3 of 6, Math.round(0.5 * 100) = 50. PENDING_APPROVAL does not count.

Never: the permission string is compared directly against the user's role

items.prompt: Several HR managers start onboarding workflows at the same moment on the SQLite deployment. What failure does the critique predict?

choices.text: Writers queue behind SQLite's single write lock, so some requests stall and fail with SQLITE_BUSY
Silent lost updates, because SQLite has no transactions
Duplicate primary keys, because SQLite cannot generate ids for concurrent inserts safely
Dirty reads, where one manager sees another manager's uncommitted tasks before the start transaction commits

choices: Writers queue behind SQLite's single write lock, so some requests stall and fail with SQLITE_BUSY
Silent lost updates, because SQLite has no transactions
Duplicate primary keys, because SQLite cannot generate ids for concurrent inserts safely
Dirty reads, where one manager sees another manager's uncommitted tasks before the start transaction commits

items.explanation: SQLite supports one concurrent writer; the multi-write start transaction holds the lock, and with no retry logic (critique item 3) the error escapes to the client.

Updates the task, logs activity, then recalculates progress as separate non-transactional calls, so progress can go stale
It recalculates progress before updating the task, so the stored value is always one step behind

choices.text: It is never delivered automatically: the setTimeout job lived only in memory, so the row stays PENDING
BullMQ replays it from Redis once Redis comes back, because the job was written to the queue before the fallback
It is delivered at boot, because server startup re-queues every PENDING email row it finds
It was already sent synchronously before the timeout was scheduled

It was already sent synchronously before the timeout was scheduled

validate(createOnboardingCaseSchema), which rejects ids from other departments

validateCaseTransition throws INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION and the task update fails
The case becomes IN_PROGRESS and completedAt is reset to null

Because the notification needs the audit event's id, which only exists after a second transaction commits
So no slow external call runs inside the transaction, and a notification failure cannot undo a committed start
